title: st.plotly_chart ignores font_family and font_color in fig.update_layout for Sankey diagrams, but fig.show() renders correctly
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Hi Streamlit team 👋

I'm experiencing an issue when displaying a Plotly Sankey diagram in Streamlit. When I use `fig.update_layout()` to customize the font — specifically `font_family` and `font_color` — these settings are not reflected in the Streamlit app using `st.plotly_chart()`. However, when I call `fig.show()`, the chart renders correctly with the intended font and color


### Reproducible Code Example

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-11031)

```Python
import streamlit as st
import plotly.graph_objects as go

fig = go.Figure(data=[go.Sankey(
    node=dict(
        pad=15,
        thickness=20,
        line=dict(color="black", width=0.5),
        label=["A", "B", "C", "D"],
        color="blue"
    ),
    link=dict(
        source=[0, 1, 0, 2, 3],
        target=[2, 3, 3, 3, 0],
        value=[8, 4, 2, 8, 4]
    )
)])

fig.update_layout(
    title="Sankey Diagram Example",
    font_family="Times New Roman",
    font_color="blue",
    font_size=14  # This is the only setting that works
)

st.plotly_chart(fig)  # Font family and color are ignored
# fig.show()          # Shows correct font and color
```

### Steps To Reproduce

_No response_

### Expected Behavior

All font-related layout settings (family, color, size) should be applied when rendering the chart via `st.plotly_chart.`

### Current Behavior

* `font_size` works ✅

* `font_family` and `font_color` are ignored ❌ when rendered in Streamlit, but work in native Plotly (`fig.show()`)

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.44.1
- Plotly version: 6.0.1
- Python version: 3.11.11
- Operating System: macOS
- Browser: Brave Version 1.74.50


### Additional Information

_No response_

Hi [USER] thank you for filing this ticket!

The theming behavior with the code written here is expected since we apply a Streamlit theme by default for a great out of-the-box experience. However, Streamlit also supports utilizing Plotly theming constructs! Utilize the `theme=None` parameter to do so. In this example, it would become `st.plotly_chart(fig, theme=None)`.

For additional documentation, take a look at our [doc pages for Plotly theming](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/charts/st.plotly_chart#:~:text=Copy-,Theming,-Plotly%20charts%20are).

Let me know if this solves the issue at hand. Thanks for using Streamlit!

Here’s what I tested: ``` fig.show() col1, col2 = st.columns(2) with col1: st.plotly_chart(fig) with col2: st.plotly_chart(fig, theme=None) ``` And here’s what I’m seeing in the Streamlit app: This is the output from`fig.show()`: Interestingly, even in the native Plotly render, the node font color doesn't change—but in the Streamlit app, the font style is noticeably different and harder to read. Let me know if I might be missing something else or if there's a workaround for the font styling in node labels.

Thanks for the update, [USER]. That explains the behavior I was seeing. I appreciate you checking it out and bringing it to the team’s attention!

[USER] if a workaround is required in the meantime, setting the font params in `textfont` in `go.Sankey` allows changing font color. ```python import streamlit as st import plotly.graph_objects as go fig = go.Figure(data=[go.Sankey( node=dict( pad=15, thickness=20, line=dict(color="black", width=0.5), label=["A", "B", "C", "D"], color="blue" ), link=dict( source=[0, 1, 0, 2, 3], target=[2, 3, 3, 3, 0], value=[8, 4, 2, 8, 4] ), textfont=dict( family="Times New Roman", color="red", shadow="", size=14 ) )]) fig.update_layout( title="Sankey Diagram Example", ) st.plotly_chart(fig) ```

This is a confirmed bug where `st.plotly_chart` ignores user-specified `font_family` and `font_color` settings from `fig.update_layout()` when displaying Sankey diagrams (and other chart types). The root cause is in Streamlit's Plotly theming implementation: the Sankey-specific template in `streamlit_plotly_theme.py` explicitly sets `textfont.color` to a placeholder color, and the frontend's `CustomTheme.tsx` uses a `merge()` operation that overwrites user values with theme defaults instead of respecting user-specified settings. The `font_size` parameter works because it's not explicitly set in the theme template. A workaround is to use `st.plotly_chart(fig, theme=None)`, but this disables all Streamlit theming.

### Related Issues

- **#7955** - [Cannot set custom st.plotly_chart() font attributes with fig.update_layout()](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/7955) - This is essentially the same bug. It reports that `st.plotly_chart` ignores font settings passed via `fig.update_layout()`, using Streamlit's theme fonts instead. Users want the option to override the theme and use custom fonts. **Likely duplicate.**

- **#4178** - [Cannot set Plotly theme because Streamlit overrides user values](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/4178) - Related issue where `st.plotly_chart` overrides user-defined Plotly templates/themes with Streamlit's theme. This is part of the same underlying problem where user customizations are not respected.

- **#12425** - [Make charts use `textColor` for all text](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12425) - Enhancement request to make chart text colors respect the global `textColor` theme setting. Related to the broader issue of font/color customization in charts.
